## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Siṅgālajātaka* (Ja 113), titled "The Jackal" in English translation, is a narrative in the Pali Jātaka collection set at the Bamboo Grove (*Veḷuvana*) near Rājagaha [SuttaCentral]. The story of the present relates to the Buddha's treacherous cousin Devadatta [SuttaCentral]. According to the narrative framework, the monks assembled in the Hall of Truth were discussing how Devadatta had led five hundred followers astray to Gayāsīsa, broken up the monastic community with false claims to the truth, and introduced his own ascetic practice of observing two fast-days per week [SuttaCentral]. Entering the hall, the Buddha declared that Devadatta was equally deceitful in past lives and recounted the story of the past to illustrate this [SuttaCentral].
In the story of the past—often characterized as the tale of the "drunken jackal"—a festival is held in honor of spirit-deities, during which meat, fish, and pots of alcohol are strewn across city streets [SuttaCentral; DeCaroli 1999]. In this tale, the Bodhisatta is reborn as a tree-spirit residing in a cemetery grove and shows no interest in the offerings, while a cunning jackal readily capitalizes on the food and intoxicating drink left unattended [SuttaCentral; DeCaroli 1999]. The tale is noted in secondary literature as a unique depiction among the Jātakas of an ancient festival honoring spirit-deities with offerings of meat and alcohol [DeCaroli 1999], and is referenced by Winternitz in his survey of Buddhist narrative literature [Winternitz 1933].
Regarding parallels and text reuse, SuttaCentral registers no curated parallels for this text in other languages, and the automated alignments computed by DharmaNexus record no internal Pali text reuse or cross-language parallels with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
